title: tenant-residency-attestation-orchestrator-with-retention-safeguards
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a Tenant Residency Attestation Orchestrator for Dedicated capacity that assembles cryptographically-signed evidence bundles (node manifests, geolocation metadata, network/zonal attestations), enforces tenant-specific retention policies, and exposes an authenticated verification API and scheduled reporting hooks for auditors. The orchestrator must operate as a fault-tolerant pipeline producing tamper-evident artifacts customers can download or validate via API. This work covers: evidence collection agents, evidence packaging and signing, retention enforcement and immutable archival, verification endpoints, console/reporting integration, and operational runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Automated evidence bundle generation for a tenant completes within 60s for a single-node snapshot and 5 minutes for full multi-node snapshot
Evidence bundles include structured manifest.json (sha256 hashes), provider-zone metadata, node certificate chain, and a detached JWS signature verifiable with a published public key

Retention settings applied per-tenant: evidence older than configurable retention period is archived to read-only long-term storage or deleted according to tenant policy; enforcement validated by integration tests
Verification API returns cryptographic verification status and signed bundle metadata; API requires mTLS and token-based auth
Console exposes a per-tenant "Download Attestation" button and a scheduled weekly attestations report; access restricted by RBAC
E2E test harness can simulate 100 concurrent tenant requests without data leakage between tenants
Operational runbook and Incident playbook added to Confluence; monitoring dashboards and alerts for pipeline failures and signing errors
tasks: Design: finalize evidence bundle JSON schema and signature format (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/residency-attestation-spec)
Infra: provision immutable object store bucket with lifecycle policies, encryption, and access logging
Security: integrate signing with KMS/HSM-backed keys; define rotation policy and key access audit
Agent: add lightweight evidence collector to Dedicated node agent to emit node manifests and zone metadata
Orchestrator: implement pipeline (collector -> validator -> packager -> signer -> archive) with retry semantics and deduplication
API: implement attestation verification endpoints and scoped download endpoints behind edge auth
Console: UI changes to show attestation status and enable ad-hoc requests for evidence
Retention: implement per-tenant retention enforcement job and audit trail events
Tests: unit, integration, and E2E tests, including fuzzed manifests to validate verification failure paths
Docs: customer-facing docs and internal runbook + example verification tooling
decisions: Use JWS (JSON Web Signature) with detached payloads for attestation signatures to maximize cross-platform verification support instead of Sigstore (sigstore evaluated but deferred due to key management constraints for POC)
Store evidence bundles in an append-only object store with immutable write-once buckets; create short-lived downloadable URLs for customer retrieval
Per-tenant signing keys will be derived from a tenant master key in KMS; actual HSM signing performed in the signing service to limit key exposure
Retention enforcement will support two modes per tenant: archive-to-long-term (immutable) and hard-delete. Archive mode keeps a signed index and audit event for compliance queries
Verification API and attestation download endpoints will require mTLS + scoped JWT; console access controlled via existing org RBAC claims
